summary: npm package ships an obfuscated fake-Cloudflare-Turnstile HTML lure with no install-time execution
details: The tarball contains a single index.html that impersonates a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' Turnstile challenge page. The HTML embeds a heavily hex-obfuscated inline IIFE (variables like _0xNNNN, string-array reassembly) that reconstructs an outbound URL at runtime via '"https://"+_0x236c01(...)'. package.json declares main=index.html, ships only index.html, and defines no preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare scripts, so npm install and require() do not execute the payload on an installer's machine. The obfuscated script only runs if the HTML file is opened or served to a browser, making the artifact a phishing/lure page hosted on the npm registry rather than a supply-chain attack against package consumers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
